The equation x2+8x−33=0 can be written in the form (x+p)2=q. Find p+q, and solve the equation.

a
p+q=49,x=−11 and x=3
b
p+q=49,x=−3 and x=11
c
p+q=53,x=−11 and x=3
d
p+q=51,x=−2 and x=3
e
p+q=53,x=−9 and x=3
Submit

decision.explanation: Completing the square gives x²+8x=33, so (x+4)²=49. Thus p=4 and q=49, giving p+q=53. Taking square roots gives x+4=±7, so x=-11 or x=3.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}+8x-33=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $\,p+q,$ and solve the equation.
after.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+8x-33 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+8x & =33 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x & =33 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x+{4}^{2}-{4}^{2} & =33 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x+{4}^{2})-16 & =33 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16 & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square and solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2}-16 & =33 \\ (x+4)^{2} & =49\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=4,q=49,$ and $p+q=53.$

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2} & =49 \\ \sqrt{(x+4)^{2}} & =\sqrt{49} \\ x+4 & =\pm 7 \\ x & =-4\pm 7\end{aligned}
$$

We simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-4+7=3 \\ x & =-4-7=-11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-11$ and $x=3.$

Question 1

The equation x2+8x−33=0 can be written in the form (x+p)2=q. Find p+q, and solve the equation.

a
p+q=49,x=−11 and x=3
b
p+q=49,x=−3 and x=11
c
p+q=53,x=−11 and x=3
d
p+q=51,x=−2 and x=3
e
p+q=53,x=−9 and x=3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side: x2+8x−33=0x2+8x=33x2+2⋅4⋅x=33x2+2⋅4⋅x+42−42=33(x2+2⋅4⋅x+42)−16=33(x+4)2−16=33

Then, we isolate the perfect square and solve the equation using the square-root method: (x+4)2−16=33(x+4)2=49

So, p=4,q=49, and p+q=53.

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

(x+4)2=49(x+4)2=49x+4=±7x=−4±7

We simplify the two solutions: x=−4+7=3x=−4−7=−11

Therefore, the solutions are x=−11 and x=3.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Quadratic Equation When the Solutions Are Rational
content.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}+8x-33=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $\,p+q,$ and solve the equation.
content.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+8x-33 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+8x & =33 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x & =33 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x+{4}^{2}-{4}^{2} & =33 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x+{4}^{2})-16 & =33 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16 & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square and solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2}-16 & =33 \\ (x+4)^{2} & =49\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=4,q=49,$ and $p+q=53.$

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2} & =49 \\ \sqrt{(x+4)^{2}} & =\sqrt{49} \\ x+4 & =\pm 7 \\ x & =-4\pm 7\end{aligned}
$$

We simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-4+7=3 \\ x & =-4-7=-11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-11$ and $x=3.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-4x+4=9$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $\,p+q,$ and the sum of the roots ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+4 & =9 \\ {x}^{2}-4x & =5 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot x & =5 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2} & =5 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot x+{2}^{2})-4 & =5 \\ (x-2)^{2}-4 & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}-4 & =5 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=-2,q=9,$ and $p+q=7.$

Now, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =9 \\ \sqrt{(x-2)^{2}} & =\sqrt{9} \\ x-2 & =\pm 3 \\ x & =2\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

We simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =2+3=5 \\ {x}_{2} & =2-3=-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=5.$ Thus, the sum is $4.$

The equation m2+8=−8m can be written in the form (m+p)2=q. Find p+q, and solve the equation.

a

decision.explanation: Rearranging gives m²+8m=-8. Adding 16 yields (m+4)²=8, so p=4, q=8, and p+q=12. Thus m=-4±√8=-4±2√2.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The equation ${m}^{2}+8=-8m$ can be written in the form $(m+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
after.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, the $-8m$ term to the left-hand side, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}^{2}+8 & =-8m \\ {m}^{2}+8m & =-8 \\ {m}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot m & =-8 \\ {m}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot m+{4}^{2}-{4}^{2} & =-8 \\ (m+4)^{2}-{4}^{2} & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+4)^{2}-{4}^{2} & =-8 \\ (m+4)^{2} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=4,q=8,$ and $p+q=12.$

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+4)^{2} & =8 \\ \sqrt{(m+4)^{2}} & =\sqrt{8} \\ |m+4| & =\sqrt{8} \\ m+4 & =\pm 2\sqrt{2} \\ m & =-4\pm 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

(m+4)2=8(m+4)2=8|m+4|=8m+4=±22m=−4±22

content.problem: The equation ${m}^{2}+8=-8m$ can be written in the form $(m+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
content.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, the $-8m$ term to the left-hand side, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}^{2}+8 & =-8m \\ {m}^{2}+8m & =-8 \\ {m}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot m & =-8 \\ {m}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot m+{4}^{2}-{4}^{2} & =-8 \\ (m+4)^{2}-{4}^{2} & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+4)^{2}-{4}^{2} & =-8 \\ (m+4)^{2} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=4,q=8,$ and $p+q=12.$

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+4)^{2} & =8 \\ \sqrt{(m+4)^{2}} & =\sqrt{8} \\ |m+4| & =\sqrt{8} \\ m+4 & =\pm 2\sqrt{2} \\ m & =-4\pm 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: The equation ${a}^{2}-12a+18=0$ can be written in the form $(a-p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
after.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}-12a+18 & =0 \\ {a}^{2}-12a & =-18 \\ {a}^{2}-2\cdot 6\cdot a+{6}^{2}-{6}^{2} & =-18 \\ (a-6)^{2}-{6}^{2} & =-18\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(a-6)^{2}-{6}^{2} & =-18 \\ (a-6)^{2}-36 & =-18 \\ (a-6)^{2} & =18\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=6,q=18,$ and $p+q=24.$

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(a-6)^{2} & =18 \\ \sqrt{(a-6)^{2}} & =\sqrt{18} \\ |a-6| & =\sqrt{18} \\ a-6 & =\pm 3\sqrt{2} \\ a & =6\pm 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$
